etymologies.etymologyHTML:
Early 16th century (originally Scots and northern English, denoting "earthenware, pot, jug"), of unknown origin, perhaps from North Germanic (compare Swedish mugg (“mug, jug”), Norwegian mugge (“pitcher, open can for warm drinks”), Danish mugge), or Low German mokke, mukke (“mug”), German Low German Muck (“drinking cup”), Dutch mok (“mug”), also of unknown origin. Perhaps related to Old English muga (“stack”) and Old Norse múgr (“mass, heap (of corn)”). Compare also Middle English mug, mog (“a measure of salt”).

"Face" sense possibly from grotesque faces on certain drinking vessels. "Assault" sense of verb possibly from hitting someone in the face.

definitions.definition: A large cup for beverages, usually having a handle and used without a saucer. A mug

quote.text: When did ever a gentleman o’ fortune show his stern to that much dollars for a boosy old seaman with a blue mug — and him dead too?

definitions.definition: (slang, derogatory) A gullible or easily cheated person.
(UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, derogatory, slang) A stupid or contemptible person.

quote.citation: 1940, United States. Congress Senate, Hearings (volume 13, page 27252)
quote.text: Perhaps if I told you that there were forty arrests made in one day here, you will realize that with this small equipment available in the Sheriff's Office, it is very difficult to get mugs. These people are being mugged as they are being arrested but with an entirely inadequate force at work prints have not as yet been made.

definitions.definition: (transitive, obsolete, UK, Ireland) To strike in the face.

quote.text: Madgbury showed game, drove Abbot in a corner, but got well Mugg'd.

quote.citation: 1857, "The Leary Man", in Anglicus Ducange, The Vulgar Tongue
quote.text: And if you come to fibbery, You must Mug one or two,
"Suppose they had Mugged you?" / "Done what to me?" / "Mugged you. Slogged you, you know."

definitions.definition: (transitive) To assault for the purpose of robbery.
(intransitive) To exaggerate a facial expression for communicative emphasis; to make a face, to pose, as for photographs or in a performance, in an exaggerated or affected manner.

quote.text: Her dress is too obviously "costume," and Ford-Smith mugs too broadly for us to forget, as we should, that Katie is a theatrical invention.
